A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SEBA study, with readable text, equations, figures and tables throughout. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both reference separate supplementary material that is not included. The supplied content supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original MuJoCo and Atari attack experiments, component ablations and targeted-attack evaluations in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experiments in Tables 1–5 and adds qualitative attack examples in Figure 2.

M1.justification: The shadow critic, GAN, world model, alternating training and targeted-attack objective remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–3. The new Double-DQN statement supplies implementation information without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same five MuJoCo tasks and three Atari games, including targeted attacks on the retained MuJoCo tasks. Figure 2 illustrates existing Cheetah Run and Walker Run settings.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across Tables 1–5: the image attacks, adapted RL attacks, Atari comparisons and targeted-attack baselines all match. Figure 2 illustrates already evaluated PGD, C&W and Square attacks.

E3.justification: Victim agents, metrics, perturbation bound 8/255, rollout horizon H=4, training budgets and targeted-action ranges remain unchanged. V2 clarifies existing ablation descriptions without establishing a revised evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: New Figure 2 provides a qualitative comparison of perturbation visibility on Cheetah Run and Walker Run. The discriminator, perturbed-state and world-model ablations and their findings remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results use 10 random seeds and mean plus standard deviation. No repeated-run counts, uncertainty-reporting practices or significance tests change.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 are identical, including rewards, FID, query costs and targeted-success rates. Figure 2 adds qualitative clean and adversarial observations supporting the existing imperceptibility finding.

T1.justification: Equations 1–13 retain the same objectives and mathematical relationships. Added hats on simulated states and the corrected perturbation notation clarify existing mathematics; no assumptions, derivations or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central novelty, attack-effectiveness, imperceptibility, query-efficiency and targeted-control claims remain the same. The conclusion rephrases cross-domain applicability without establishing a different contribution or scientific scope.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations of baseline difficulties, discriminator function, critic distribution mismatch and the world model's efficiency tradeoff. No substantive limitation or applicability boundary is added or removed.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the supplementary-code statement with a specific repository pointer and identifies the shadow-critic update as Double-DQN. It clarifies that the no-world-model variant uses real rollouts for both networks, but removes the statement that targeted success is measured over full evaluation episodes.

R1.justification: V2 adds seven distinct cited works, including Rainbow and CGAR, and expands discussion of previously cited adversarial-RL research. The main research positioning remains unchanged. Duplicate Korkmaz and Double-Q bibliography entries do not represent additional distinct works.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the visual-RL related-work summary, reformats baseline descriptions, shortens some explanations and adds author notes and acknowledgements. The main section sequence and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figure 2 and revises Figure 1's arrows, transition tuple and stage-update labels to better match the existing algorithms. Table 3 moves alongside Tables 4–5 on page 8, with associated text and reference reflow.

improvement.justification: Figure 2 adds inspectable visual evidence, Figure 1 corrects explanatory labels, and the repository pointer and implementation disclosure improve usability. These gains are limited because quantitative validation is unchanged. Removing the full-episode success-rate statement slightly reduces protocol detail, but does not outweigh the modest improvements.
